title: Porridge and the Glowing Crumbs
markdown:
Whoooo… settle in now, dear listeners, and let old Hoot tell you a story. The moon is a sliver of light tonight, just like the beginning of a new adventure. And this story begins, as many good things do, with quiet evenings and a very special friendship.

Once upon a time, in the quiet and tall Frostcap Range, there lived a young ogre named Porridge. Porridge was not like other ogres. He wasn't loud or boastful. Porridge was as gentle as a field of sleeping daisies, with a heart that glowed as warmly as the fire in his cave. His cave always smelled of pine needles that had danced in the wind and the comforting scent of a warm fire. Every single day, Porridge would help his mum. Together, they would gather the softest moss, like fluffy green clouds, to make their beds just right, and collect plump, juicy berries, red and blue, for their supper. And Porridge’s very best friend, the keeper of forest secrets, was a crow named Pip. Pip had feathers so black and shiny, they looked like tiny pieces of the deepest night sky had fallen and stuck to him. And his eyes? They sparkled with mischief and all the clever news he’d gathered. Pip’s caws were like little chuckles carried on the breeze, full of important tidbits. "Whoooo knew," Porridge would often say, a slow smile spreading across his broad, kind face, "that a little crow could know so much about our woods?"

Every day unfolded like a soft, familiar song. Porridge would carefully, oh so carefully, place the plump berries into his little woven basket, making sure none tumbled out. And Pip, Pip would perch on a branch just above. He tilted his head. He listened to the forest whisper and rustle. "The squirrels are being extra busy today, Porridge," Pip would chatter, his voice a flurry of tiny sounds. "Burying their nutty treasures, they are! And Mrs. Badger is knitting a lovely new scarf for her littlest cub. Can you smell the sweet clover, Porridge? It's extra strong today. Whoooo can smell it?" Porridge would take a deep breath, filling his lungs with the crisp, clean mountain air, feeling safe and happy, snug in the world he knew. It was a good, peaceful kind of rhythm.

Until one evening, as the moon, a magnificent silver cheese wheel, began its slow climb into the inky sky, Porridge felt a little adventurous. He decided to take a tiny wander, just a little stroll. The bluebell woods, usually so quiet and dim at twilight, seemed to be playing a game with the moonlight, shimmering and sparkling. He wasn't looking for anything special, just enjoying the cool air kissing his cheeks and the sweet, damp smell of the earth after a gentle day. And then, he saw them. Little, tiny crumbs. And each one left a faint, friendly glow on the mossy path. A tiny tremor rippled through Porridge's whiskers. *This is surprise,* he realised. "Oh my goodness," whispered Porridge, his eyes growing as wide as saucers. "What curious little lights! They’re like tiny fallen stars!"

Because of that, Porridge couldn't help himself. He started to follow the trail of glowing crumbs. They winked and twinkled, like little secrets being shared by the path, leading him deeper and deeper into the whispering woods. The trees here were much taller, their branches like sleepy, ancient arms reaching up to tickle the sky. And the air… the air grew sweeter, carrying a new, delightful smell. It was like honey mixed with freshly baked bread, a scent that made Porridge’s tummy give a little happy wiggle. Porridge, who usually knew his way around like the back of his own big hand, felt a tiny bit unsure as the path wiggled and jiggled. He wondered what he would find. The smell was so lovely, he couldn't wait! But the glowing crumbs ahead, so cheerful and inviting, beckoned him onward.

Because of that, Porridge found himself standing at the entrance of a most unusual place. It was a cozy den, shaped like a plump, friendly mushroom. A warm, golden light spilled from its round window, and that wonderful smell of honey and warm bread was even stronger here. Cautiously, very carefully, Porridge peeked inside. And there, beside a warm, happy oven, was a little goblin! He wore a flour-dusted apron and was humming a merry little tune. He was busy placing cookies, made from those very same glowing crumbs, onto a cooling rack. Porridge’s tummy rumbled, a soft, polite little rumble. He loved cookies, oh yes he did. But he also remembered his mum’s gentle reminder to always stay close to home, where it was safe and familiar. A tiny flutter, like a butterfly’s wing, began to beat in his chest. He felt a little bit worried about being so far away.

Because of that, the goblin baker looked up. His eyes twinkled just like the glowing crumbs! He didn't seem surprised at all to see a young ogre peeking into his cozy den. "Well now, hello there, young sir!" he chirped, his voice sounding like the crinkle of a new storybook page. "Have you perhaps lost your way, little one? These crumb cookies, you see, they have a bit of a wanderlust themselves! They do love to lead folk on little adventures." He then held out a cookie. It still pulsed with a gentle, warm light, and was just the right size for a curious ogre. "Here," the goblin said kindly. "Try one. They'll make you feel right as rain, I promise." Porridge carefully took the cookie. It was warm in his hand. When he took a bite, it tasted like sunshine and happy thoughts all mixed together. A tiny sigh of pure joy escaped him. The goblin, with a smile that crinkled his nose, then pointed a floury finger down a clear path. "That way, my friend," he said. "It will take you straight back to the big, friendly cave you know. Your friend Pip will be waiting for you, no doubt at all."

Until finally, with Pip, who had been looking everywhere and landed with a reassuring caw right on his shoulder, Porridge trotted down the path. The glowing crumbs had vanished, but the memory of their soft light and the delicious taste of the cookie lingered. The moon seemed to smile down at him, a big, gentle circle in the sky, and the familiar scent of pine needles grew stronger and stronger. He could almost hear the soft, cozy crackle of his own cave fireplace. Porridge felt a warm wave of relief wash over him, like being wrapped in his softest blanket. The forest itself seemed to sigh a happy, contented sigh as he hurried towards home.

Ever since then, Porridge knew. He knew that even if he followed a trail of enchanting, glowing crumbs, and even if he wandered a little farther than he had planned, the path back to his cozy cave, and the love of his family, was always waiting. It was always safe and warm, like the most delicious bowl of stew you could ever imagine. Whoooo could ever ask for anything more? And the trees remember this story well, they do.
